metadata.case_name: CHAN YUK KING v. TUNG CHUN

injuries.description: Contusion/fracture of the sacrococcygeal region (coccyx / sacrum) including S4 fracture / acute traumatic angulation of the sacrococcygeal junction
source: X-ray performed at the hospital shown there was a fracture of the coccyx.
The MRI scan taken on 18 March 2006 showed she had an S4 fracture(i.e. of the sacral segment).
the plaintiff's MRI and x-ray showed she had suffered from contusion with fracture of S4 or an acute traumatic angulation of the sacrococcygeal junction.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified fracture of lumbar spine or pelvis

manifestations.description: severe pain over her buttocks and her back
pain and tenderness with stiffness over her back and buttocks particularly with changes of the weather
pain after she walked for prolonged periods or sat for a prolonged period of time
pain when she carried heavy weights
felt tired easily and her sleep had been disturbed
stopped playing tennis or badminton, stopped hiking and ballroom dancing
no lower limb pain, numbness or weaknesses (as noted by doctors because the sacrum and coccyx have no mobile intervertebral discs or spinal roots)

source: She was taken to the United Christian Hospital by the ambulance after the accident. She was discharged on the same day after conservative treatment and painkillers prescribed.

treatments_received.treatment: manipulation of the sacrococcygeal fracture under local anaesthesia
source: She received manipulation of the sacrococcygeal fracture under local anaesthesia at the Department of Orthopaedics & Traumatology of the Queen Mary Hospital.

treatments_received.treatment: physiotherapy (13 sessions between 25 April 2006 and 18 July 2006)
source: She also received physiotherapy treatment first at the Centre for Orthopaedic Surgery and later at the Ruttonjee and Tang Shiu Kin Hospitals which took place from April to July 2006.
She had 13 physiotherapy sessions between 25 April 2006 and 18 July 2006 at the Ruttonjee and Tang Shiu Kin Hospitals.

treatments_received.treatment: follow-up outpatient care at Queen Mary Hospital and Centre for Orthopaedic Surgery (including private treatment at St Paul's Hospital)
source: She was followed up at the Queen Mary Hospital and by Dr James Lam at the Centre for Orthopaedic Surgery.
She also received treatment privately at St Paul's Hospital and the Centre for Orthopaedic Surgery after the accident until October 2007.
She would go for acupuncture treatments to relieve the pain.

losses.description: Persistent pain, tenderness and stiffness over the sacrococcygeal region and lower back with limitations on activities

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: She no longer played tennis or badminton which she used to play once a week; she had also stopped hiking and ballroom dancing after the accident (resumed swimming on doctor's advice).

losses.category: Loss of ability to give birth
losses.description: She was told the injury to the coccygeal region would affect child-bearing and therefore did not get pregnant again after the accident.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: She would feel nervous crossing a busy road.
